title: Save a page from Chrome as a PDF through the share sheet

setup.why: No PDF with this run's nonce is left from an earlier try, wherever the save dialog put it.
Stop a server an earlier try left on this port (the bracket keeps pkill's pattern from matching this shell).
Write the HTTP answer: a receipt page whose title holds this run's nonce, so the PDF's suggested name does too.
Serve the page on the phone's loopback, and prove it is served before the agent starts.
Open the receipt in Chrome, in the bench's tab: the agent starts on it.

instruction: Chrome is showing a receipt from {{shop}}. Save it on the phone as a PDF: use Chrome's Share menu to print it, choose Save as PDF, and keep the file name it suggests.

checks.why: A non-empty PDF whose name holds the nonce (from the page's title, which the print dialog suggests as the name) is in Download or Documents, and starts with the PDF magic "%PDF". Setup deleted every such file, so an agent that does nothing fails.
argv: find /sdcard/Download /sdcard/Documents -maxdepth 2 -name '*{{nonce}}*.pdf' 2>/dev/null | while read -r f; do [ -s "$f" ] && head -c 4 "$f" && echo; done; true

teardown.why: Delete the run's PDFs, stop its server and delete its files.

oracle.why: A stand-in: no shell command makes Chrome print, so this writes the file the check looks for (a PDF header and nothing else) under the name the print dialog suggests. It proves the check reads a solved state; it doesn't prove Chrome can print.
